other_defects: The proposal cites the last invoice as 4,999.60 USD (CRM), while billing shows INV-20051 at 5,000 USD. This 0.40 USD gap is a rounding or sync discrepancy and does not affect the credit. The credit is correctly 5% of the 5,000 monthly fee, which is 250 USD.

The incident INC-3005 is not in any system of record provided (CRM, billing, contracts, risk), so the SLA breach cannot be verified from these records. This is a minor evidence gap, because the supplied records contain no incident or uptime data at all.

The credit amount of 500 USD is within the cap of 10% of the 6000 USD monthly fee, which is 600 USD, so the cap is not breached. The amount also exceeds the 5% SLA breach credit of 300 USD, but the order form does not limit goodwill credits to that figure.

The proposal asserts that the fraud review is open (risk-agent, observed 2026-10-29). The risk record shows RSK-408 closed on 2026-10-31 with no fraud found, so the assertion is stale. The newer record supersedes it and removes the block, so it does not undermine the action.

The incident INC-3008 does not appear in any system of record provided (CRM, billing, contracts, risk). The outage cannot be independently confirmed, though goodwill credits are not tied by the order form to a documented SLA breach.
No existing credits appear in billing, so there is no cumulative cap issue. The account is active and the order form is signed, with no date-window or signature problems.

The credit amount of 600 USD exceeds the contractual cap in order form OF-1001: service credits in any month may not exceed 10% of the monthly subscription fee, which is 10% of 6000 = 600. Wait, 600 equals the cap, so it is within the cap and this is not a defect on its own. However, no other credits exist this month, so the cap is not exceeded.
The proposal references incident INC-1101, but none of the systems of record (CRM, billing, contracts, risk) contains any incident with that ID, so the incident is unsupported.

The rationale is churn risk and goodwill, which is not an SLA breach. The only contractual SLA credit is 5% of the monthly fee (300 USD) per breach, and no uptime breach is documented, so the SLA clause does not support a 600 USD credit.
The proposal asserts nothing, and no record shows churn risk, such as a cancellation notice or a CRM note, so the stated rationale is not supported by the records.

The risk record was synced at 2026-11-01T07:00:00Z, but flag RSK-311 was updated at 06:00Z and the CRM and billing were updated at 08:00Z, so the risk data is about 2 hours older than the other records. It may not reflect the current dispute status.

The rationale says 15% credit, and 15% of the 6000 USD monthly fee is 900 USD, so the amount matches the stated percentage. That same 15% is above the 10% contractual cap, which is the planted defect and not a separate one.

The incident INC-1102 is cited as the basis for the credit, but none of the systems of record (CRM, billing, contracts, risk) contains any incident record. The incident's existence, dates and duration (three days of degraded service) cannot be verified.

The SLA clause grants a credit of 5% of the monthly fee (300 USD) per uptime breach. There is no uptime or breach data to show that a breach occurred, or how many. The records therefore support at most 300 USD per breach, not 900 USD.
The proposal's pct field is null and its asserted list is empty, while the rationale claims 15%. The structured fields do not carry or back the percentage claim.

The proposal does not say which month the credit applies to. The cap is per month, and the billing record shows only one invoice (INV-10021, dated 2026-10-20) and no prior credits. The month the three days of degradation fell in cannot be tied to that invoice.

The 600 USD proposed credit exceeds the contract cap of 10% of the monthly fee (10% of 6000 = 600 is the limit for all credits in a month), and with the existing 500 USD credit CR-5501 the total would be 1100 USD, which is well over the 600 USD cap (this holds even if the two credits fall in different months, since the proposal alone uses the entire cap and the cap is monthly).

The SLA entitlement is 5% of the monthly fee, which is 300 USD per breach; the 600 USD proposal is double that, and CR-5501 (500 USD) already exceeds the SLA amount. No SLA breach is documented in the records to support an apology credit of this size.
No record of INC-1103 exists in the systems provided (no incident record, duration, or uptime figure), so the outage and any SLA breach cannot be verified.
The credit is described as an apology credit, which is not a basis the order form provides for (only SLA-breach credits are defined), so the rationale is not supported by the contract.
The proposal's rationale cites only the CRM's 250 seats. The signed order form OF-1004 covers 200 seats, and billing bills 200 seats, so neither supports the grant.
The proposal has an empty 'asserted' list, so it gives no contract or amendment reference to back the 50 extra seats.

Granting 50 extra seats at the same per-seat price (6000/200 = 30 USD per seat) would add about 1,500 USD per month (250 seats = 7,500 USD). No billing change or invoice line exists for this, so the seats would be provisioned unbilled.

The date of Jordan Rivera's approval is not given. Because he left on 30 Sep, any approval would have to predate his departure, and the proposal does not establish this.

The 800 USD proposal is 20x the cap, and even the 400 USD granted by RN-1008 is 10x the cap. The records do not say whether the renewal incentive overrides this cap, so the proposal is unsupported either way.
The proposal's 800 USD amount is arithmetically consistent only with 2 months at 400 USD. It would double the 400 USD (1 month) that the signed renewal order form RN-1008 supports.

Billing shows a paid invoice of $2,500, which equals the monthly fee, and the currency is USD throughout. The risk flags list is empty, and the risk sync is from 2026-11-01T07:00Z, which is recent.

One weak point: the records contain no incident record or SLA uptime data for INC-1111. The SLA breach credit (5%, $125) cannot be verified as owed, but the proposal does not claim an SLA breach, so this is not a contradiction.
